clue.text: Communist comrades? They could make you laugh

definitions.meaning: playfully, the brothers of Karl Marx, the father of communism
the ... were a celebrated American comedy team

explanation.surface: Fellow communists, it is suggested, could be a source of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is whimsical: brothers of the communist Marx, rather than political comrades.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho, Chico, Harpo and Zeppo made a string of classic film comedies.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about horse — one finally ran

indicators.note: about says the word for enthusiastic is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: mad about something means enthusiastic about it
a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: finally says only the closing letter of the word one is used

explanation.surface: A keen racing fan watches a horse that finally ran.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it, so ran and managed are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Bird with yellow head hidden

indicators.note: with its head hidden the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, which is craven

explanation.surface: A bird with a yellow head is out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow head' looks like a bird's plumage, but yellow is cowardly, CRAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Most awkward attempts to enter bar

indicators.note: to enter says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bolt bars a door
a shy is an attempt or throw, so shies are attempts

explanation.surface: The most awkward customers keep trying to get into the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British slang for uncooperative or difficult, so the superlative is most difficult.

clue.text: City going up in thick smoke

indicators.note: going up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the city's letters lie concealed inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A city is disappearing upwards in thick smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the concealment: 'in' supplies it. In a down clue 'going up' turns the letters found across 'thick smoke' upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large Siberian city in Russia.

clue.text: Heavenly body the fellow's to look at endlessly

parts.note: the fellow's becomes he's, with the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to peruse is to look at closely

explanation.surface: A man gazing at a star seems never to stop looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperus is the evening star, the planet Venus seen in the west after sunset.

clue.text: Gentleman upset about newspaper quarrels

indicators.note: about says the reversed title is wrapped around the paper
upset in a down clue turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight, a gentleman
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A gentleman is upset by newspaper stories about rows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is a breach in a relationship, a falling-out, so rifts are quarrels.

clue.text: One won't easily change misguided trades union sacking ten

indicators.note: misguided says the letters are to be rearranged
sacking says certain letters are fired from the pool before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A union clinging to old ways sacks ten workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, E, N from TRADES UNION and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinosaur is a person stuck in outdated ways, resistant to change.

clue.text: Shout about former US President offering goodness!

indicators.note: about says the shout goes round the president

parts.note: to cry is to shout
Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Someone yells about an ex-president's virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, used interchangeably.

clue.text: Unorthodox love isn't ending in happiness — in our stories?

indicators.note: unorthodox suggests the letters are arranged in an unconventional way
ending in says only the final letter of happiness is taken

explanation.surface: Unconventional love stories still end happily in fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the people whose work lies behind the tales we read.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of fiction are the creators behind the narratives we read.

clue.text: What is ad for? Nothing should be a false story

indicators.note: should be says one letter is replaced by another piece

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a lie is a false story

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader asks what an advert is for, suspecting a fabrication.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a leaflet handed out as advertising.

clue.text: My wild beast beginning to gallop around, showing enthusiasm

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the beast are jumbled

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

indicators.note: beginning to says the first letter of gallop is taken
around says the exclamation is turned the other way

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like oh

explanation.surface: An onlooker exclaims as a wild beast starts galloping about with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the beast's name and 'around' turns the exclamation the other way; the surface pairs 'My' with the beast, but it is a separate exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho means zealously eager, often recklessly so.

clue.text: Writer having block — what can get the flow going?

definitions.text: what can get the flow going?

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
a stock is a block of wood, such as the stocks for punishment or a gun's wooden stock

explanation.surface: A writer with writer's block wonders what will get the words flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests creative flow; the definition means water.
explanation.definitionFit: A penstock is a sluice or channel controlling water to a mill wheel or turbine.

clue.text: One herding animals runs into port

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cattleman runs into a port town.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover drives livestock to market over long distances.

clue.text: Bit of an old LP providing a limited mindset?

definitions.meaning: a single song on a long-playing record
a ... mind fixes on one thing only

explanation.surface: A song from an old album suggests narrow thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: One-track describes thinking obsessed with a single subject; literally, a single recording on an album.

clue.text: Crime — something dazzling almost in part of Greater Manchester

indicators.note: in says the glare piece sits inside the town

parts.note: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: glare is dazzling light

explanation.surface: A crime involving something sparkling, perhaps jewellery, takes place near Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: BURY is a town in Greater Manchester, a metropolitan county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglary is breaking into a building to steal, a criminal offence.

clue.text: Ace dancing with glamour putting Romeo off — saucy type

indicators.note: dancing says the letters move about into a new order
putting with off says a letter is removed from the pool
off with putting says that letter is removed from the pool

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancing ace sheds a lover's glamour and turns cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R from ACE GLAMOUR and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Guacamole is an avocado-based dip, a kind of sauce; saucy here means of the sauce variety, not cheeky.

clue.text: Before the last word comes short sad complaint

indicators.note: before says the shortened word comes ahead of the other piece
short says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: grave means serious and sombre
amen ends a prayer, the last word

explanation.surface: A sad complaint is uttered just before someone has the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravamen is the essence of a grievance, a legal term for the grounds of a complaint.

clue.text: Exhaust in specific location of US vehicle

definitions.meaning: to exhaust is to tire someone too much

definitions.text: in specific location of US vehicle
definitions.meaning: over the tire, using the American spelling of tyre, is a place on a car

explanation.surface: An exhaust is fitted to a particular spot on an American car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' suggests the car's tailpipe but is a verb. The second reading splits the answer as OVER TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtire someone is to wear them out completely.

clue.text: Mysterious copper squashed between two officers

indicators.note: squashed between says the metal is placed between the two officers

parts.note: OC is officer commanding and LT is lieutenant
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman is mysteriously sandwiched between two senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Occult means hidden or supernatural, beyond ordinary understanding.

clue.text: Grass that may bend over with no effect

indicators.text: that may bend over with no effect
indicators.note: turning it back to front changes nothing, as the word reads the same both ways

parts.note: the grass named here is the sand-dune species, whose name is its own wordplay

explanation.surface: A grass bends in the wind without any lasting effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass planted to stabilise sand dunes.

clue.text: Therapist has service on foreign street set up

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: set up in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A therapist offers a service on a street abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur treats patients with massage, a form of physical therapy.

clue.text: Remedy offered by minister, one very small to be swallowed

indicators.note: to be swallowed says the pieces go inside the minister

parts.note: a curate is an assistant minister in the church
I is the Roman numeral for one
v is the abbreviation for very, written small as a lower-case letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers a cure, a tiny pill to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A curative is a medicine or treatment that heals.

clue.text: Mostly gentle, a river that divides counties

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tame means gentle and docile
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mostly gentle river forms the boundary between counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall, counties of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar forms most of the boundary between the counties of Devon and Cornwall.

clue.text: Wild animals not provided with right tags

indicators.note: not provided with says the letter is taken away

parts.note: badgers are wild animals

explanation.surface: Wild animals lack the correct identification tags.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges are emblems or labels worn to identify someone.

clue.text: It's remarkable anger being voiced

indicators.note: being voiced says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to grate is to irritate or anger

explanation.surface: It is remarkable that someone's anger is being expressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means outstanding or notable.

clue.text: Drink cold Guinness maybe

parts.note: ale is a drink
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A drink, served cold, could be Guinness.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness looks like the stout, but it is the actor Sir Alec Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec Guinness was the British actor of Star Wars and Ealing comedies, an example of the name.

clue.text: I stand in watering-hole having demolished a litre with little hesitation

indicators.note: having demolished says those letters are removed

parts.note: a local is a neighbourhood pub
um is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub, having downed a litre, hesitates a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The LOCAL is a British term for one's regular nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily substitutes for another.

clue.text: Inspirational female wants strain reduced by half when leading old blokes in gym

indicators.note: when leading says the halved word comes first
reduced by half says only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a strain is a tune or melody

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the gym

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym lessons
men are blokes

explanation.surface: An inspiring woman wants her strain relieved by half when leading old men at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Melpomene is the Muse of tragedy, and the Muses inspired artists.

clue.text: Place in poem given award by cheeky Charlie years ago

parts.note: a grant is an award of money
Charlie Chester was a British comedian billed as Cheerful Charlie, popular decades ago

explanation.surface: A spot in a poem is given a prize by an old cheeky comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie Chester was a British radio and TV comedian of the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Grantchester is the village near Cambridge in Rupert Brooke's poem The Old Vicarage, Grantchester.
